WOODS RUN DIGEST

Thursday edition

November 26, 2026

TENNESSEE — DRYING AND PLANING / NOVEMBER 24 ANNOUNCEMENT

C-Wood targets faster drying and a larger finished-lumber business

C-Wood Lumber plans to invest US$21.5 million in a kiln and dried-lumber planer facility at its existing Collinwood, Tennessee, location. The state’s November 24 announcement projects 25 new jobs, doubling the workforce, and monthly capacity rising from 1.2 million board feet to more than five million.

The new kiln is expected to shorten drying from seven to nine days to 24 hours or less. Those are project targets, not measured results from an operating expansion. C-Wood began as a sawmill in 1983 and shifted exclusively to lumber drying in 1989. The investment concerns drying and finishing lumber, rather than an announced increase in the company’s own log-sawing capacity. The release gives no completion date or new supplier terms.

Tennessee’s original expansion announcement →

By the Numbers

Latest available observations as of 2026-11-26. Dates and comparison periods vary by series; monthly figures remain unchanged between releases.

IndicatorLatestChange
U.S. on-highway dieselEIA U.S. on-highway diesel; taxes includedUS$5.70/galWeek of November 23, 2026; released November 24−US$0.24/gal
−4.1%Versus November 16: US$5.94/gal
Lumber futuresJanuary 2027 lumber futures (CME LBRF27)US$550.00/MBFNovember 25, 2026 settlementUnavailableNovember 18 same-contract settlement not independently verified; checked November 26
Madison’s lumber indexMadison’s weekly lumber indexUS$440.00/MBFWeek ending November 20, 2026−US$4.00/MBF
−0.9% (calculated)Versus week ending November 13: US$444.00/MBF
Hardwood lumber PPIBLS WPU0812; 1982=100; not seasonally adjusted284.3 index pointsOctober 2026; released November 13−1.3 points
−0.4%Versus September 2026: 285.6
U.S. single-family housing startsCensus U.S. single-family starts; annualized estimate864,000 units (SAAR)October 2026; released November 18+33,000 units (SAAR)
+4.0%Versus revised September 2026: 831,000
Canadian dollarBank of Canada; Canadian dollars per U.S. dollarC$1.42 per US$1.00Daily average, November 25, 2026−C$0.01 per US$1.00
-0.5%Versus November 24: C$1.43 per US$1.00; Canadian dollar strengthened

Housing starts are annualized estimates, not actual monthly units, and are subject to revision. The hardwood PPI is an index, not a dollar price. Exchange rates are daily averages. MBF means thousand board feet. The October single-family starts monthly change has a published ±9.0-percentage-point 90.0% confidence interval and is not statistically significant. The named January 2027 contract table verifies US$550.00 for November 25. The continuous historical series shows a different price and is not substituted; the November 18 named-contract settlement was not independently confirmed. Display rounding follows the approved format. Changes are calculated from unrounded observations, so rounded currency levels may look unchanged even when a small movement occurred.

Sources:
EIA U.S. on-highway diesel; taxes included
Investing.com named-contract table
Madison’s November 20 index
BLS hardwood lumber PPI via FRED
Census U.S. single-family starts; annualized estimate
Bank of Canada daily averages

Curtailment Watch

Sexton Lumber’s Bloomfield, Newfoundland, operation is bringing crews back after its October fire. In CBC’s November 24 interview, reproduced by Tree Frog Forestry News, owner Kevin Sexton said woods crews were harvesting again and about half the mill crew had returned. He hoped to have a full crew back the following Monday. This is a reported ramp-up, not confirmation of full production or a new log-buying commitment. CBC: owner interview on the return to work · Tree Frog: attributed November 24 interview excerpt

Equipment & Markets

U.S. / CANADA — EQUIPMENT / NOVEMBER 25 OUTLOOK

Deere sees a flat global forestry-equipment market in 2027

Deere’s November 25 earnings presentation forecasts roughly flat global forestry-equipment industry demand, measured in units, for fiscal 2027. Its outlook for U.S. and Canadian construction equipment is different: flat to five percent growth.

The company’s combined Construction & Forestry division reported fourth-quarter sales of US$3.793 billion, up 12%, while operating profit fell to US$339 million from US$348 million. The division includes construction and other equipment, so that sales increase is not a stand-alone forestry result. For logging-equipment buyers, the useful distinction is between a mixed business’s reported sales and management’s separate, forward-looking forestry-market forecast.

Deere’s dated earnings presentation, pages 10–12 →

Action Detector

CANADA — NEW BRUNSWICK / PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

Arauco’s St. Stephen air-quality renewal goes to public review

New Brunswick began a 180-day public participation process November 25 for renewal of Arauco Canada’s Class 1 air-quality approval in St. Stephen. The mill makes medium-density fibreboard and particleboard from hardwood chips, softwood shavings and other residual wood fibre. Its current operating approval expires June 30, 2027.

The province’s public-review portal links the facility profile, current approval and notice, with instructions for written comments and questions to the Authorizations Branch. This is review of an existing mill’s operating terms, not an expansion announcement or a new residual-fibre purchasing offer. The portal is also where draft terms and responses to issues raised during consultation will appear.

New Brunswick’s November 25 notice → · Facility documents and public participation instructions →

Under the Radar

ALASKA — FOREST MANAGEMENT / NOVEMBER 24 ADOPTION

Haines gets an adopted forest plan and new land classifications

Alaska adopted the Haines State Forest Resource Management Area Management Plan and Land Classification Order SE-24-001 on November 24. The plan and order affect approximately 280,000 acres of state-owned, state-selected and top-filed lands; that figure is the planning area, not acres opened for timber harvest.

The final plan consists of the public-review draft with the recommended revisions. The new order supersedes earlier land-classification orders within the boundary. The state links those documents and its response to substantive public comments, giving foresters and other land users the adopted planning framework rather than a new timber-sale prospectus.

Official adoption notice and final-plan access →

This illustrated book profiles the loggers and small businesses working in New York’s Adirondack forests. Its photographs and firsthand accounts show varied approaches to equipment, markets, family businesses and making a living in the woods.
